role.altitude: The week stays with family-program consults, tenant demonstrations, rule explanations, and food conversations. The assistant gains no right to change a family program, skip a demonstration, waive a rule, or set a diet.
reach: Child, Family, and School Social Workers
skills_to_grow: Confirm the source record before a draft or a price comparison runs.
Refuse a kept point when the record does not contain that point.
Keep the nutritional judgement apart from the price arithmetic.

tasks.short: Consult with supervisor concerning programs for individual families.

steps.what: Read the family program record before the consult
Read supervisor mail about this family program
Draft program points the family record already names

loop.input: The family program record opened in the previous read.
loop.output: Draft program points whose program name is already in that record.
loop.check: Keep a point only when that program name appears in the record text.
loop.stop: One pass, then stop. If no name matches, the draft is empty and nothing is written.
loop.why_not_simpler: A case title does not state which program applies to this family.

steps.what: Check that each program point matches the family record
Consult with supervisor concerning programs for individual families

tasks.design: The assistant still reads the family program record in {OTHER} and the supervisor mail in {EMAIL}. A bounded loop in {DOCS} drafts only program points that record already names, and the assistant checks that each point matches the record. The consult stays a conversation with the supervisor and writes nothing back.
tasks.previous_blocker: The program that applies sits in free text, so a fixed report could not tell which point to take.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded extract can keep a point only when the record already names that program, and stop with an empty draft.
tasks.still_hard: The consult still turns on the family's situation, which the record does not settle.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant and the supervisor decide which program to discuss. The draft does not.
tasks.altitude: Preparation loses the scan of program names already in the record. The consult stays the same length, and the assistant gains no right to set the program.

reach.role: Child, Family, and School Social Workers
reach.task: Prepare a family program discussion from the record
reach.learn: Which program name must already be in the record, and that the draft must not decide eligibility.

evidence.claim: Keeping a program point only when the family record already names it does not choose the program.
Health data are a special category under article 9.
Article 22 means no eligibility decision based solely on automated processing.
Annex III 5(a) covers eligibility for public assistance, including healthcare, by or for public authorities.
Recording staff conversations needs works council consent.

assumptions: Published means sum to 99.9. Floors are screens 4, spreadsheets 0, mail 6, documents 15 and meetings 72, which is 97. Three extras go to mail (remainder 0.9), documents (0.7), then screens. Screens and spreadsheets both have remainder 0.6, and screens comes first in the means order, so spreadsheets stay at 0. The missing tenth is not invented.
No spreadsheet is used. The family program record is a client dossier in {OTHER}, not an employee record. Supervisor mail is {EMAIL}. The points are drafted from {DOCS}.
Workflow boundary: the assistant prepares and holds the consult. The supervisor decides the program. Nothing is written back to the dossier.

Structured input from s1: family identifier, program name, and program status. If the program name is absent, the draft is empty and the assistant uses the record in the consult. Native search is tried first; the loop runs only because the name sits in free text.
The actor on every step, including the draft, is the social service assistant, who gathers those points today. The machine appears only as the future fate of that draft.

The consult is with a colleague, so it is not an outside send. It is not recorded, so the works-council rule on recording staff conversations is not triggered. Nothing is sent or committed, so no approval gate is opened. The check still happens before the assistant relies on the draft, and the consult does not edit accepted program points v1.
This draft does not determine eligibility for public assistance. The family record can hold health data, so access is treated as special-category data.
Focal incremental upkeep is zero. The meaning check sits inside s4. One system hour keeps the program-name extract current. When the draft is empty, the low end of the range is zero.
unknowns: Whether the family program record stores the program name as text the assistant can open.
research_questions: Which fields of the family program record are text, and which are scans?

already_counted.description: The assistant checks that each kept program point matches the family record. That time sits in s4.

incremental.description: Keep the program-name extract current when the family record changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low when the record names no program and the draft is empty, so the consult is unchanged. High when most kept points match and only the 8-point draft is shortened. The consult stays at full time.

tasks.short: Demonstrate use and care of equipment for tenant use.

steps.what: Read the equipment note for this tenant visit
Read the mail that names the tenant visit
Draft care steps the equipment note already states

loop.input: The tenant equipment note opened for this visit.
loop.output: Draft care steps that the note already states.
loop.check: Keep a step only when the same sentence appears in the equipment note.
loop.stop: One pass, then stop. If the note states no care step, the draft is empty and nothing is written.
loop.why_not_simpler: The equipment name does not state the care steps.

steps.what: Check that each care step is stated in the note
Demonstrate use and care of equipment for tenant use

tasks.design: The assistant still reads the housing equipment register in {OTHER} and the visit mail in {EMAIL}. A bounded loop in {DOCS} drafts only care steps the equipment note already states, and the assistant checks each step against that note. The demonstration to the tenant stays in the room and sends nothing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Care steps are sentences on the equipment note, not a fixed list the assistant could set once.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded extract can keep a step only when that sentence is already in the note.
tasks.still_hard: Showing the tenant how to use the equipment still happens in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant sees whether the tenant can use the equipment. The draft does not.
tasks.altitude: A short scan of care sentences leaves the note. The demonstration stays the same length, and the assistant gains no right to skip it.

reach.task: Show a client how to use home equipment
reach.learn: Which care sentence must already be in the equipment note before it is shown.

evidence.claim: Copying a care step the equipment note already states does not decide how to demonstrate it.
Health data are a special category under article 9.

assumptions: Published means sum to 100.1. Floors are screens 3, spreadsheets 0, mail 1, documents 7 and meetings 87, which is 98. Mail remainder 0.9 takes the first extra. Spreadsheets remainder 0.5 would take the second. That point is refused because this demonstration uses no spreadsheet and no spreadsheet baseline is invented. It goes to documents, the next remainder at 0.4. Result: screens 3, spreadsheets 0, mail 2, documents 8, meetings 87. The extra tenth in the published sum is not allocated.
The housing equipment register is the {OTHER} category. Visit mail is {EMAIL}. Care steps are taken from the note in {DOCS}.
Workflow boundary: the assistant demonstrates to the tenant. No handout is produced and nothing is written to a dossier.

Structured input from s1: equipment name and care sentence. If the note has no care sentence, the draft is empty and the assistant demonstrates from the note in the room. The loop runs because the care sentence is free text, after a plain search returns nothing.
The actor on every step, including the draft, is the social service assistant, who reads those care steps today. The machine appears only as the future fate of that draft.

The demonstration is to a tenant, outside the organisation, so the live step is an external action. It releases no artefact, so no approval gate is opened. The check still happens before the assistant relies on the draft, and the demonstration does not edit accepted care steps v1.

A care sentence may name a health condition, so access to the note is treated as special-category data. The loop copies stated steps and does not decide the demonstration. Literacy for that loop applies now.
Focal incremental upkeep is zero. The meaning check sits inside s4. One system hour keeps the care-sentence extract current. An empty draft is the low end of the range.
unknowns: Whether the housing equipment register stores a care sentence for each item the tenant uses.
research_questions: Are care sentences text in the equipment note, or only a name of the item?

already_counted.description: The assistant checks that each care step is stated in the equipment note. That time sits in s4.

incremental.description: Keep the care-sentence extract current when an equipment note changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low when the note states no care step and the draft is empty. High when most of the 4-point draft matches the note. The demonstration stays at full time.

tasks.short: Explain owner or management rules such as sanitation or parking.

steps.what: Open the property screen for sanitation and maintenance requirements
Read the visit mail about parking regulations
Quote rule sentences the owner document already contains

loop.input: The owner rule document and the topic named in the visit mail.
loop.output: Quoted sentences on sanitation, maintenance, or parking that the document already contains.
loop.check: Keep a sentence only when that sentence appears in the owner document and names sanitation, maintenance, or parking.
loop.stop: One pass, then stop. If no sentence matches, the draft is empty and nothing is written.
loop.why_not_simpler: One clause can mention both parking and maintenance, so one keyword does not pick the sentence.

steps.what: Check that each quoted sentence is the rule meant
Explain rules established by owner or management

tasks.design: The assistant still opens the property screen in {OTHER} and reads the visit mail in {EMAIL}. A bounded loop in {DOCS} quotes only sanitation, maintenance, or parking sentences the owner document already contains, and the assistant checks that each sentence is the rule meant. The explanation to the tenant stays spoken.
tasks.previous_blocker: Owner rules mix sanitation, maintenance and parking in prose, so one keyword pulled the wrong clause.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded quote can keep a sentence only when that sentence is in the owner document and names one of those topics.
tasks.still_hard: Whether this tenant gets an exception is still said in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant decides how to say the rule to this tenant. The quote does not waive it.
tasks.altitude: Less time goes to finding the sentence in the rule document. The spoken explanation stays the same length, and the assistant gains no right to waive a rule.

reach.task: Explain a house rule that touches health, such as sanitation
reach.learn: Quote the stored sentence, and leave any exception to the person speaking with the resident.

evidence.claim: Quoting a sentence the owner document already contains does not decide an exception for this tenant.

assumptions: Published means sum to 100.0. Floors are screens 3, spreadsheets 0, mail 6, documents 20 and meetings 68, which is 97. Remainders are screens 0.8, documents 0.7, spreadsheets 0.6, meetings 0.6 and mail 0.3. The first extra goes to screens and the second to documents. The third would go to spreadsheets, because spreadsheets precedes meetings on the tied 0.6. That point is refused: these rules are not kept in a spreadsheet, and no spreadsheet baseline is invented. It goes to meetings. Result: screens 4, spreadsheets 0, mail 6, documents 21, meetings 69.
The property screen is the {OTHER} category and only identifies the document. The rules themselves are in {DOCS}. Visit mail is {EMAIL}. No posted notice is created.
Workflow boundary: the assistant explains the rule to the tenant. Nothing is sent and nothing is written to a record.

Structured input: property identifier from s1, topic from s2, and the clause text in the owner document. If no sentence matches, the draft is empty and the assistant explains from the document in the room. A plain keyword is not enough when one clause names two topics, so the loop is the extract.
The actor on every step, including the quote, is the social service assistant, who finds those sentences today. The machine appears only as the future fate of that quote.

The explanation is to a tenant, outside the organisation, so the live step is an external action. It releases no artefact, so no approval gate is opened. The check still happens before the assistant relies on the quotes, and the explanation does not edit accepted rule sentences v1.
The rules are public house rules, not an eligibility decision and not health data. Literacy for the quote loop applies now.
Focal incremental upkeep is zero. The meaning check sits inside s4. One system hour keeps the sentence extract current. An empty draft is the low end of the range.
unknowns: Whether sanitation, maintenance and parking rules sit in one owner document the assistant already opens.
research_questions: Are those rules prose in one document, or separate notices the task does not name?

already_counted.description: The assistant checks that each quoted sentence is the rule meant for this visit. That time sits in s4.

incremental.description: Keep the rule-sentence extract current when the owner document changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low when no sentence matches and the draft is empty, so the explanation uses the document as today. High when most of the 11-point quote matches. The spoken explanation stays at full time.

tasks.short: Observe food selections and recommend economical nutritional choices.

steps.what: Observe clients food selections before any comparison
Read stored prices and diet limits for this client
Read the household budget note from the mail
Subtract listed prices for the observed food selections
Check the prices and name the nutritional choice
Recommend alternate economical and nutritional food choices

tasks.design: The assistant still observes the food, then reads stored prices and diet limits in {OTHER} and the budget note in {EMAIL}. A deterministic comparison in {DOCS} subtracts only prices the price note already lists, and drops any item with no listed price. The assistant checks those prices, names the nutritional choice, and recommends it in the room. Nothing is written to the client record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Price arithmetic was mixed into the nutritional judgement, and the prices were not subtracted on their own.
tasks.enabler_now: Where a price note already lists the price, ordinary subtraction can do that arithmetic and leave the food choice to the assistant.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing what the client chose, and judging a nutritional alternate, stay in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant sees the food in front of the client and names the alternate. The comparison only shows prices.
tasks.altitude: The price subtraction leaves the visit. Observation and the recommendation stay the same length, and the assistant gains no right to set a diet.

reach.task: Recommend a food choice from what the client has
reach.learn: Separate a listed-price subtraction from the nutritional judgement, and make that judgement in the room.

evidence.claim: Subtracting a price the price note already lists does not decide which food is nutritional.
Health data are a special category under article 9.

assumptions: Published means sum to 100.0. Floors are screens 1, spreadsheets 0, mail 2, documents 10 and meetings 85, which is 98. Spreadsheets remainder 0.8 would take the first extra. That point is refused because this visit uses no spreadsheet and no spreadsheet baseline is invented. The two extras go to screens and meetings, which tie at remainder 0.4. Screens comes first in the means order, and both receive a point. Result: screens 2, spreadsheets 0, mail 2, documents 10, meetings 86.
Meetings time splits into observation 40 and the recommendation 46. Both stay at full remaining time. Documents split into the price subtraction 5 and the assistant's check 5.

Stored prices and diet limits are on the client record in {OTHER}, not an employee record. The budget note arrives in {EMAIL}. The comparison is worked in {DOCS}. No price table is invented beyond notes the assistant already opens.
Workflow boundary: the assistant observes and recommends in the room. The comparison does not write a diet note.

Structured input: item name from the observation in s1, price and unit from s2, budget figure from s3. An item with no listed price is left out of the comparison. If no price is listed, the assistant compares by hand and still names the choice. The subtraction is deterministic and uses no model loop.
The actor on every step, including the subtraction, is the social service assistant, who does that arithmetic today. The machine appears only as the future fate of that subtraction.

Observation is watching, not a send. The recommendation is to the client, outside the organisation, so that live step is an external action. It releases no artefact, so no approval gate is opened. The check names the choice before the recommendation, and the recommendation does not edit accepted food choices v1.

Diet limits are health data. The comparison does not decide nutrition. Focal incremental upkeep is zero. The judgement sits inside s5. One system hour keeps the listed prices current. When no price is listed, the low end of the range is zero.
unknowns: Whether a price note already lists a price for the foods this client buys, and whether diet limits are on the client record.
research_questions: Who keeps the listed prices current, and how often a visited item has no price?

already_counted.description: The assistant checks the prices against the diet limit and names the choice. That time sits in s5.

incremental.description: Keep the listed prices current when the price note changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low when no observed item has a listed price, so the assistant does the arithmetic as today. High when most items have a listed price and most of the 5-point subtraction is shortened. Observation and the recommendation stay at full time.
